h1: The 6 Best Printers for Mac and MacBook Users, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Mac: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 printers for Mac and MacBook users compared on AirPrint, macOS drivers, ink tanks, duplex printing and document feeders.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the printer to buy for a Mac household that prints mostly text, thanks to AirPrint, a full macOS driver, duplex printing and a 250-sheet tray. The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 is the best choice if you also scan and want cheap ink, the ET-2800 is the lean EcoTank, and the Brother MFC-J1360DW has a color screen for easy AirPrint setup.
intro: A Mac does not need a printer driver the way a Windows PC does, and that is both the good news and the trap. AirPrint lets a MacBook print to almost any wireless printer with no software, but it exposes only the basic options. If you want to pick a paper tray, set a print quality, tweak a duplex mode or scan from the Mac, you need the maker's full macOS driver. The right printer for a Mac supports both.

We reviewed seven printers from their spec sheets and listings, ranking them on AirPrint support, full macOS driver availability, duplex printing, document feeders, ink or toner cost structure and setup. Mac compatibility claims come from the listings, so check the maker's driver page for your macOS version before you buy. Price buckets replace exact prices.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A monochrome laser with AirPrint, a full macOS driver, duplex and a 250-sheet paper tray.
products.description:
Brother's DCP-L2640DW is a monochrome laser with AirPrint compatibility, a full macOS driver, automatic duplex printing and a 250-sheet paper tray. It sits in the $200 to $500 range.

For a Mac user who prints documents, this is the cleanest fit. AirPrint gets you printing in seconds, and the full driver unlocks tray selection and scanning from the Mac when you need them. Toner does not dry out between jobs, which matters for an occasional printer, and the 250-sheet tray means reloading is rare. The limit is color: it prints in black and white only, so presentations and photos are out.

Buy it if your printing is mostly text and you want the least maintenance. Skip it if you print color regularly.
cons: Prints in black and white only
products.idealFor: Mac households that print mostly text.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: A cartridge-free ink tank all-in-one with AirPrint, a document feeder, Ethernet and fax.
products.description:
The ET-4800 uses Epson's refillable ink tanks instead of cartridges, supports AirPrint, includes an automatic document feeder, and connects over Ethernet or wireless. It scans, copies and faxes, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Two things make it a smart Mac choice. The wired Ethernet port is a fallback when wifi misbehaves, which is a common cause of the printer offline message on a Mac. The ink tanks lower the cost per page sharply compared with cartridges, so a Mac home office that prints color and black pages will spend far less on ink over a year. The feeder handles stacks of scans. The trade is a larger, heavier body than a cartridge inkjet.

Buy it if you print and scan often and want low running cost. Skip it if you have very little desk space.
pros: Ink tanks cut cost per page
Ethernet port as a wifi fallback
cons: Refilling tanks is a messy step
products.idealFor: Mac home offices that print and scan weekly.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: A cartridge-free tank printer with AirPrint, a full macOS driver, scanning and copying.
products.description:
The ET-2800 is the simpler EcoTank, with a cartridge-free ink tank system, AirPrint compatibility, a full macOS driver and scan and copy functions, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks below the ET-4800 only because it lacks a document feeder and a wired port. For a Mac household that prints regularly and does not scan stacks, those extras are not needed, and the ink savings come with a smaller price. Owners of tank printers also avoid the problem of cheap cartridges that run out in a week of heavy use.

Buy it if you print regularly and want lower long-run ink cost. Skip it if you scan multi-page documents often.
products.idealFor: Regular Mac printers who do not scan stacks.

products.name: Brother Work Smart MFC-J1360DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: A 1.8 inch color display, AirPrint, automatic duplex and a full macOS driver in a mid-priced inkjet.
products.description:
The MFC-J1360DW has a 1.8 inch color display, AirPrint compatibility, automatic duplex printing and a full macOS driver. It uses cartridges and sits in the $100 to $200 range.

A color display is a practical help during AirPrint setup. You can see the printer join the network, read its IP address and check for errors without opening a computer. Duplex is automatic, and Brother's driver gives a Mac user the full set of options. It ranks fourth because it is a cartridge printer, so running costs are higher than the EcoTank models.

Buy it if you want an on-device screen and a capable inkjet. Skip it if per-page cost matters most.
cons: Smaller feature set than tank models
products.idealFor: Mac users who like an on-device screen.
products.skipIf: You print enough to want cheaper ink.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A budget AirPrint printer with a feeder, fax and the Canon PRINT app for extra settings.
products.description:
The TR4720 supports AirPrint, includes an automatic document feeder and a built-in fax, and works with the Canon PRINT app for extra settings. It is the low-price option in the $50 to $100 bracket.

AirPrint makes setup on a Mac simple, and the Canon PRINT app adds some of the settings that plain AirPrint hides. The feeder and the fax are unusual at the price. It ranks fifth because it is a standard cartridge printer, so ink gets expensive with volume, and because the listing does not mention a full macOS driver.

Buy it if you are a budget Mac household that wants simple AirPrint. Skip it if you print more than a few dozen pages a month.
pros: Feeder and fax at a low price
cons: Full macOS driver is not listed
products.idealFor: Budget Mac households with light printing.
products.skipIf: You print heavily or want a full driver.

products.name: Canon TS5320 All-in-One Wireless Printer with AirPrint
products.verdict: AirPrint support is advertised outright, with Alexa support and the Canon PRINT app.
products.description:
The TS5320 advertises AirPrint support, works with Alexa and the Canon PRINT app, and is Amazon Dash Replenishment ready. It is a wireless all-in-one in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Its selling point for a Mac user is the explicit AirPrint claim in the title, which removes doubt. Alexa support lets you start a print by voice if you use a smart speaker. The Dash Replenishment feature is of limited use now that the service has been scaled back, so treat it as a minor detail. It ranks sixth because it costs more than the TR4720 without clear advantages for Mac printing.

Buy it if you want AirPrint confirmed in the title and like voice control. Skip it if you want a feeder or duplex.
products.idealFor: Mac users who want confirmed AirPrint and Alexa.

whatMatters.detail: AirPrint lets a Mac print with no software but offers only basic options. A full macOS driver adds tray selection, quality modes and scanning. Look for the words full macOS driver or Mac driver on the listing, not just AirPrint.

Cartridge inkjets are cheap to buy and costly to feed. Tank printers like the EcoTank models cut the cost per page sharply, and lasers use toner that lasts for thousands of pages. Estimate your yearly pages before you choose.

A Mac sometimes shows a printer as offline when wifi drops or the router changes. An Ethernet port, as on the ET-4800, gives you a stable alternative. It is a small feature that avoids a big annoyance.
Automatic duplex printing saves paper, and a feeder scans stacks without lifting the lid. They matter most in a home office. Check for the word automatic, since manual duplex is a chore.
A color screen helps you see the network status and fix errors without a computer. Without one, you rely on lights and the Mac's Printers and Scanners settings. A guided setup saves time.

faq.q: Do I need to install a driver on my Mac?
faq.a: Not for basic printing. AirPrint prints with no software. For tray selection, quality modes and scanning, install the maker's full macOS driver, which the Brother and Epson models list.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake Mac users make when choosing a printer?
faq.a: Assuming AirPrint means full control. It handles basic printing, but advanced settings need a driver. Choose a printer with a full macOS driver if you want paper tray and quality control.

faq.q: Is an EcoTank worth it over a cheaper cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print weekly, yes. The ink tanks cut the cost per page sharply. For a few pages a month, a cheap cartridge printer costs less overall.

faq.q: How hard is setup on a Mac?
faq.a: Connect the printer to wifi from its display or app, then add it in System Settings under Printers and Scanners. Most Macs find AirPrint printers automatically within a minute.

faq.q: Why does my Mac say the printer is offline?
faq.a: It usually means a wifi dropout or a changed IP address. Restart the printer and router, or re-add the printer. An Ethernet port, as on the ET-4800, avoids most of these problems.

faq.q: Does the laser printer work with Apple Silicon Macs?
faq.a: AirPrint works regardless of processor, and Brother lists a full macOS driver. Check the maker's driver page for your macOS version, since support can change with major updates.

finalTake: For text-heavy Mac users, the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best printer here, with AirPrint, a full macOS driver and duplex. The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 suits home offices that scan and want cheaper ink, and the ET-2800 is the lean version. The Canon TR4720 is the budget AirPrint pick. Check for a full macOS driver, not just AirPrint.
